description: The sampler declares a SECOND candidate plan 64 wide beside the deployment's own (--max-candidates, normally 1024) and runs a batch on it only when EVERY active chain row has an explicit 1 <= top_k <= 64. Nothing about admission changes: max_candidates stays the bound, top_k > 64 is still admitted and served by the wide plan, and top_k = 0 -- which means 'the whole candidate width' and therefore a different sampling support at either width -- keeps the WHOLE batch wide. The narrow plan is the same ops at a smaller n_cand over the same buffers' layout, so the exactness argument is per stage rather than per value: sample_topk ranks by logit and writes its live set into the same low slots, its sort reads n_cand only as an upper bound on k; the four cuts and the pick reduce with fixed 256-lane block_sum/block_max trees in which candidate slot i is its own lane at either width, and a tail hole contributes exp(-inf - mx) = 0.0f to a sum and nothing to a max -- 0.0f being the exact additive identity, no lane partial moves; the sequential top_p and inverse-CDF walks are prefixes over candidate order and the removed holes are strictly above every live index; and under tensor parallelism the merge selection-sorts world_size * n_cand gathered pairs, skipping id < 0, with keep bounded by the row's top_k and not by the buffer width. Numerics are therefore bitexact where the plan is accepted, by that construction and not by measurement; the parent's two-width pipeline comparison is what would confirm it on a device. Declaring the narrow plan costs one more set of transient candidate planes and one more declaration per stage; it allocates nothing on the step path, adds no synchronisation or readback, and a narrow plan that fails to resolve leaves the flag with nothing to do rather than failing declare. Default-off: unset, has_narrow_plan() is false, rad_kernel_count does not grow and every selection is the build's existing one.
